terms.comment: A thousand agrees like any number: mīlle hominēs, a thousand people. From two thousand on, the plural mīlia is a noun and takes the genitive (see below). mīlle with a genitive is the rarer use.

terms.grammar: noun, third declension, plural (dat. and abl. mīlibus), with the genitive
terms.comment: duo mīlia hominum, two thousand people; tria mīlia passuum, three miles (three thousand paces).

phrases.latin: Mīlle annōs, tata? Quam multōs! — Multōs vērō, immō plūrimōs.
phrases.english: A thousand years, Dad? So many! — Many indeed; very many.
phrases.source: Libellus II, Sintra: castellum et puteus

phrases.latin: nam dē mīlle fabae modiīs cum surripis ūnum, damnum est, nōn facinus, mihi pactō lēnius istō
phrases.english: for when you steal one peck from a thousand pecks of beans, it is a loss, not a crime, to me, by that milder reckoning

phrases.latin: ac prīmō placidum aequor mīlle nāvium rēmīs strepere
phrases.english: and at first the calm sea roared with the oars of a thousand ships

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency: p. 253.
